headline: Models resolve noncoding variant effects on regulation across cell types and lineages
label: Regulatory Variant Effect Modeling
summary: Recent models score regulatory variants at genome scale, from 6.48M precomputed gnomAD effects to 302,830 lineage-resolved noncoding variants.
synthesis: The common thread is fitting genetic-effect models to donor, cell-type, and sequence structure to quantify how noncoding variation perturbs regulation. jaxQTL applies negative binomial count models to pseudobulk single-cell eQTL mapping and reports more eGenes than linear models, including distal ones. ChromBPNet scores 302,830 noncoding variants across 17 hematopoietic cell types, describing lineage-structured accessibility effects complementary to GWAS. AlphaGenome 2 predicts cell-type-conditioned regulatory activity and variant effects from 1-Mb DNA, with an enhancer-gene link atlas. PrediXSKAT embeds PrediXcan-predicted expression into the SKAT kernel to jointly test rare coding and common cis-regulatory variants. Evo2VED provides precomputed Evo2 scores for 6.48M gnomAD variants. What is new is the combination of count-aware modeling, joint coding and regulatory testing, and lineage-resolved variant scoring, with sequence-to-activity prediction now extending to cell-state conditioning.
